newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev falls on peg-linked dlr shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev falls on peg-linked dlr shortcovering.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell further to 1,590-1,595 per dollar at 0800 GMT following comments that the lev may be pegged to an anchor currency under a currency board arrangement as soon as this week, dealers said.
"Comments that the lev could be pegged by the end of the week triggered a protective shortcovering by some traders while foreign currency supply dwindled," a bank dealer said.
The lev opened at 1,580 to the dollar, down from 1,570-1,572 per dollar at Monday's close.
Uncertainty among market makers about the exact rate of exchange that would be chosen to peg the lev also were a reason for building up foreign currency positions.

Finance Minister Muravei Radev said on Monday Bulgaria may peg the lev to an anchor currency at a fixed exchange rate this week as part of preparations to introduce a currency board system from July 1.
He declined to say which the anchor currency would be.
But Radev said last week that an exchange rate of 1,600 levs per dollar or 1,000 per mark was assumed in this year's budget.
Details of the budget frame were expected to be announced later on Tuesday.
The Economy Institute of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences proposed also on Monday to peg the lev to the German mark at an exchange rate between 1,300 and 1,400.
"If the lev is pegged at 1,000 per mark this week, you would get around 10 percent yield from your marks, which now trade around 920 levs," another dealer said.
The mark was bid at 916-917 levs and was offered at 920-923. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
